# TraderDaddy Pro — Developer API & MCP Server

> TraderDaddy Pro is an options-flow and market-intelligence platform. The Developer API is a paid, read-only REST + MCP (Model Context Protocol) surface that lets you pull the same institutional options flow, gamma exposure (GEX), unusual activity, screeners, sector rotation, congressional trades, earnings flow, and long-term/dividend data your subscribers see — directly into your own tools or into an AI assistant (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor).
>
> This file is a complete, LLM-friendly reference. Human docs: https://www.traderdaddy.pro/developers

New to this? Read the **Quick Start for beginners** section first. It walks you from "I just installed Claude and paid for the add-on" to "my AI can pull live market data" in a few minutes — no coding required.

Never edited a config file before? There is a fully spelled-out, click-by-click version of that same setup at https://www.traderdaddy.pro/learn/mcp-setup — where the key lives, one numbered path per app, and what a working connection looks like.

---

## What you get

- **REST API** — 30+ HTTPS endpoints returning JSON. Good for scripts, dashboards, alerts, spreadsheets, automations.
- **MCP server** — one endpoint that plugs TraderDaddy Pro into an AI assistant so you can just *ask* for the data in plain English ("what's the unusual options flow on AAPL today?", "which dividend stocks go ex-div this week?").
- Both use the **same API key** and share the **same 30-requests/minute** limit.
- Everything is **read-only**. The API cannot place trades, move money, or change your account. It only reads market data.

## Who it's for

- Traders who want live flow/GEX/screener data inside Claude, Cursor, or their own scripts.
- People automating research for a strategy — e.g. wheel-strategy monitoring, DCA timing, dividend-capture, earnings positioning. (See the **Example: wheel & dividend workflow** section.)
- Developers building trading tools, alerts, or dashboards on top of TraderDaddy Pro data.

---

## Getting access (pricing & steps)

The Developer API is a **standalone product**. It does NOT require a Premium trading subscription -- a free account can subscribe to it directly.

1. **Create a free account** — https://www.traderdaddy.pro/register
2. **Subscribe to the Developer API** — **$49.99/mo standalone**, or **$29.99/mo** while you also hold a TraderDaddy Pro subscription. Billed separately from the platform. If you cancel the platform subscription later, the API moves to $49.99/mo from its next invoice. In the app: **Settings → Developer tab** (https://www.traderdaddy.pro/settings?tab=developer).
3. **Generate an API key** — on the Developer tab, click "Generate API Key". Keys are prefixed `td_live_`. **The full key is shown only once** — copy it somewhere safe (a password manager). You can hold up to **5 active keys** and revoke any of them anytime.
4. **Start using it** — either paste the key into your AI assistant's MCP config (below) or send it as a header in REST calls.

The **MCP server is included** with API access — no separate purchase.

---

## Authentication

- **Base URL:** `https://api.traderdaddy.pro/api/v1`
- **REST auth:** send your key in the `X-API-Key` header on every request.
- **MCP auth:** send your key as `Authorization: Bearer td_live_...` (the `X-API-Key` header also works).

```bash
curl -H "X-API-Key: td_live_your_key_here" \
  "https://api.traderdaddy.pro/api/v1/unusual-activity?minScore=85&timeFrame=today"
```

Keys are never exposed to the browser and are hashed at rest — only a short prefix is stored in clear. Treat your `td_live_` key like a password.

## Rate limits

- **30 requests per minute per key** (REST calls and MCP tool calls both count against this).
- Every response includes: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix timestamp when the window resets).
- Exceed it and you get `HTTP 429`; wait until `X-RateLimit-Reset` and retry.

## Error handling

Errors return JSON: `{ "error": "...", "message": "..." }`.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | OK — data in the response body |
| 400 | Bad request — missing/invalid query parameters |
| 401 | Unauthorized — API key missing or malformed (`td_live_` prefix required) |
| 403 | Forbidden — key doesn't have permission / API access inactive |
| 429 | Rate limit exceeded — retry after `X-RateLimit-Reset` |
| 500 | Server error — contact support if it persists |

---

## Quick Start for beginners — connect Claude to TraderDaddy Pro (no code)

This is the fastest path if your goal is "let my AI assistant read live market data." You only need your `td_live_` key.

### Claude Desktop (the Claude app)

Claude Desktop can't call a remote HTTP server directly, so it bridges through a small helper called `mcp-remote` (this needs **Node.js** installed — get it from https://nodejs.org).

Open Claude Desktop → **Settings → Developer → Edit Config**, and add this to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "traderdaddy": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y", "mcp-remote",
        "https://api.traderdaddy.pro/api/v1/mcp",
        "--header", "Authorization: Bearer td_live_your_key_here"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Replace `td_live_your_key_here` with your real key, save, and **fully restart Claude Desktop**. You'll see a tools/plug icon appear. Now just ask: *"Using TraderDaddy, show me today's unusual options activity with a score above 85."*

### Claude Code (the CLI)

Run this one command (swap in your key):

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http traderdaddy \
  https://api.traderdaddy.pro/api/v1/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer td_live_your_key_here"
```

Then start `claude` and ask for market data directly.

### Cursor

Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "traderdaddy-pro": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.traderdaddy.pro/api/v1/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer td_live_your_key_here" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Browser-based clients (TradingView AI Chart Copilot and similar)

Some MCP clients run inside the browser — notably AI Chart Copilot, the Chrome
extension that adds an AI side panel to TradingView charts. These let you attach
your own MCP server, which puts TD Pro's dealer gamma, unusual flow and apex
levels next to the chart you're already reading.

In the client's MCP-server settings, add a server with:

- **URL:** `https://api.traderdaddy.pro/api/v1/mcp`
- **Auth:** either a header — `Authorization: Bearer td_live_your_key_here`
  (or `X-API-Key: td_live_your_key_here`) — or **OAuth**, if the client offers
  it. With OAuth you paste your key once on our consent page instead of storing
  it in the client's config.

Both paths land on the same 29 tools and the same 30/min limit.

Once connected, you don't write code — you ask. The assistant picks the right tool, calls it with your key, and explains the result. Tool calls count against your 30/min limit.

---

## MCP tools (29 read-only tools)

Ask your assistant for any of these in plain English; it maps your question to the right tool.

**Market & sentiment**
- `get_market_stats` — index put/call ratios, sentiment, overall market health.
- `get_market_health` — 7 macro-regime detectors (risk appetite, breadth, volatility) rolled into one read.
- `get_put_call_ratios` — put/call ratio for one ticker you name, from its nearest weekly expiration (open-interest fallback when intraday volume is thin). `putCallRatio` and `sentiment` are both `null` when there is no call volume to divide by.
- `get_conviction` — Community Conviction gauge (0–100 blend of how TD Pro traders lean on a ticker).

**Options flow**
- `get_unusual_activity` — real-time unusual options activity with scoring and sentiment.
- `get_institutional_activity` — most active tickers by institutional options-flow volume today, with directional bias.
- `get_directional_flow` — the session's cumulative (from-open) delta-weighted flow lean per underlying (cumΔ, conviction, bullish/bearish/balanced bias); pass a symbol or get the top-15 leaderboard.
- `get_dark_pool` — rolled-up off-exchange ("dark pool") equity BLOCK flow for a ticker: print count, gross and net notional, accumulation vs distribution split, largest print. The lean is inferred, not confirmed direction — it describes months of desk positioning, so distribution means a patient seller (stalling/sideways), not a short signal. Aggregates only — individual prints are not served.
- `get_sector_flow` — options flow aggregated by GICS sector ETF with sentiment breakdown.
- `get_earnings_flow` — pre-earnings unusual positioning for tickers reporting soon.

**Gamma exposure (GEX) & levels**
- `get_gex_overview` — gamma exposure across tracked symbols, flip points, key walls.
- `get_gex_ticker` — gamma exposure for any single ticker; also flags a `gammaPocket` (positive/negative) when the name's dealer gamma diverges from the broad-market regime.
- `get_apex_levels` — composite "magnet" strike ranking (OI walls + net gamma) with the gamma-flip level.

**Volatility & structures**
- `get_iv_rank` — self-relative IV rank (is a ticker's premium rich or cheap vs its own history?). Every reading carries a `source`; `ivPercentile` is present only on a `self_tracked` reading.
- `get_strategy_ideas` — ranked, auto-assembled multi-leg option structures priced off the live chain.
- `get_edge_xray` — whole-chain rich/cheap grade for one expiration, with an optional trade-archetype lens.
- `get_hedge_analysis` — ranked downside-protection structures (collars, puts, spreads) for a share position you specify.

**Screeners & signals**
- `run_screener` — run a named screener at defaults (bullish-pullback, momentum, volatility-squeeze, small-cap, volatility-surge, gamma-scan, csp-wheel, leaps, leveraged, daily-cuts).
- `get_bounce_signals` — Bounce Finder: recently detected oversold-bounce candidates with scoring.
- `get_bounce_score` — on-demand oversold-bounce composite score for one ticker.
- `get_premarket_gappers` — Warrior "5 pillars" momentum gap scan (gapping hard, has-news, low float, $1–$100, high premarket relative volume), runnable on the pre-market or after-hours tape. `rvol` is DERIVED — premarket volume ÷ 10-day average FULL-day volume, i.e. what fraction of a normal day has already traded. It is NOT TradingView's regular-session relative volume, which is meaningless before the bell. The news pillar is served as a boolean `hasNews` only; headline text, source, and article links are not redistributed.

**Intelligence, events & long-term**
- `get_politician_trades` — congressional "Power Players" most-active disclosure leaderboard.
- `get_politician_trades_by_ticker` — every congressional disclosure trade for a single ticker.
- `get_insider_trades` — Form 4 insider trades of $25k+ filed with the SEC over the past 90 days, market-wide or filtered to one ticker. Every row carries a `direction` (`buy`/`sell`/`other`); the `direction` param defaults to `buy`, pass `sell`, `other` or `all` for the other sides (`other` is awards, gifts and tax withholding — not trades in either direction). Every response also carries `available` — `{buy, sell, other}` counts for the whole 90-day window before the filter, so `count: 0` on a `buy` query is distinguishable from no insider activity at all.
- `get_short_interest` — official FINRA short data for a ticker: bi-monthly short interest (days-to-cover, current short position) plus the latest daily Reg SHO short-volume ratio (short activity is squeeze/positioning context, NOT a bearish signal).
- `get_economic_calendar` — macro events (FOMC, CPI, NFP) with consensus estimates.
- `get_long_term_quality` — fundamental quality + dividend screener across the optionable universe.
- `get_dividend_calendar` — upcoming ex-dividend calendar with yields and pay dates.
- `get_ipo_scanner` — the pipeline from pre-IPO chatter to freshly-listed names.

---

## REST endpoint reference

All paths are relative to `https://api.traderdaddy.pro/api/v1`. All require the `X-API-Key` header.

### Options Flow
- `GET /unusual-activity` — real-time unusual options activity with scoring and sentiment.
  - Params: `timeFrame` (hour|today|yesterday|3days|week|month, default today), `type` (SWEEP|BLOCK|SPLIT|GOLDEN_SWEEP), `sentiment` (BULLISH|BEARISH|NEUTRAL), `ticker`, `minPremium` (dollars), `minScore` (0–100), `page` (default 1), `pageSize` (max 100, default 10).
- `GET /flow/summary` — top tickers ranked by net premium and volume.
  - Params: `days` (0=today, 1–30, default 3), `minPremium` (default 20000), `limit` (max 500, default 50), `tickers` (comma-separated).
- Dark pool (off-exchange block flow): use the `get_dark_pool` MCP tool above — it returns window aggregates, not a per-print tape. Platform page: `/dark-pool` (Premium; 25 most liquid tracked names). No standalone REST endpoint in the public API.

### Market Data
- `GET /market-pulse` — AI-generated market sentiment narrative, updated through the session.
- `GET /market-stats` — index put/call ratios, sentiment, market-health metrics.
- `GET /put-call-ratios` — put/call ratios for SPY, QQQ and IWM from each one's nearest weekly expiration. Add `/:ticker` for any other symbol. `putCallRatio` and `sentiment` are both `null` when there is no call volume to divide by.

### Gamma Exposure (GEX)
- `GET /gex/market/overview` — GEX for tracked index symbols (SPX, SPY, QQQ) with flip points and walls.
- `GET /gex/:symbol` — GEX analysis for any ticker (computed on-demand for non-tracked symbols).
- `GET /gex/:symbol/historical` — historical GEX time series (tracked symbols only).
- `GET /gex/:symbol/apex` — Apex Levels: proximity-weighted OI walls + net gamma scored 0–100, with the gamma-flip level. Optional `expiration` (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `GET /gex/:symbol/apex/trend` — multi-day Apex trend, one point per trading day. Param `days` (1–90, default 30).
- `GET /gex/:symbol/apex/history` — intraday Apex history for the current session plus previous close.

### Sector Analysis
- `GET /sectors/flow` — options flow aggregated by GICS sector ETF (net premium, sentiment, top tickers).
- `GET /sectors/:etf/flows` — drill-down: every flow that contributed to a sector's net activity (e.g. XLK, XLF, XLE).

### Signals & Scanners
- `GET /signals` — technical breakout/continuation signals. Params: `type` (BREAKOUT|CONTINUATION), `ticker`.
- `GET /bounce-finder` — reversal-finder signals from a 9-component composite score.
- `GET /screeners/:id/run` — run a named screener. `id`: bullish-pullback | momentum | volatility-squeeze | small-cap | volatility-surge | gamma-scan | csp-wheel | leaps | leveraged | daily-cuts.

### Earnings & Events
- `GET /earnings` — earnings calendar with expected-move estimates. Params: `week` (true=this week), `date_from`, `date_to` (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `GET /earnings-flow/flow` — pre-earnings unusual positioning. Params: `days`, `minFlows`.
- `GET /economic-calendar` — macro events (FOMC, CPI, NFP) with consensus estimates.

### Intelligence
- `GET /politician-trades` — congressional STOCK Act disclosures. Params: `window` (days, default 90), `limit`.
- `GET /insider` — Form 4 insider trades ($25k+, past 90 days), each row labelled with its side. Params: `direction` (`buy`|`sell`|`other`|`all`, default `buy` — `other` is awards, gifts and tax withholding), `ticker` (filter to one symbol), `limit` (1–200, default 100). Response includes `available: {buy, sell, other}` — pre-filter counts for the whole window, so an empty `buy` result still tells you whether the ticker had sales.
- `GET /institutional/buys-sells` — institutional buying/selling by ticker with conviction. Params: `weeks` (1–52, default 2), `minConviction`, `limit` (1–200, default 50).
- `GET /institutional/sector-rotation` — net institutional flow direction by sector.
- `GET /institutional/divergences` — tickers where institutional positioning diverges from price.
- `GET /institutional/etf-options` — ETF institutional options positioning snapshot.

### Ticker Search
- `GET /ticker/search?query=...` — symbol search by name or ticker fragment.
- `GET /ticker/:symbol` — price, technicals, and options analytics for any symbol.
- `GET /ticker/:symbol/fundamentals` — market cap, P/E, EPS, revenue, float, and more.

### Long Term & Dividends
- `GET /long-term/quality` — ranked Quality Score (0–100): profitability, balance-sheet safety, valuation, payout safety. Params: `minScore`, `minDivYield`, `sector`, `sort` (score|divYield|marketCap|pe), `limit` (default 100, max 500).
- `GET /long-term/quality/:symbol` — Quality Score + full fundamental breakdown for one ticker: margins, balance-sheet safety, growth, valuation, next earnings + ex-dividend dates, company profile (`industry`, `founded`, `website`, `sharesOutstanding`), and forward-looking valuation (`forwardPE`, `enterpriseValue`, `revenueTTM`, `eps`, `epsForward`).
- `GET /long-term/dividends` — upcoming ex-dividend calendar (ex-div date, pay date, rate, yield). Params: `from` (YYYY-MM-DD), `days` (default 60, max 365), `limit` (default 200, max 500).
- `GET /long-term/sectors` — distinct sectors available in the quality dataset.

---

## Code examples

### cURL
```bash
curl -H "X-API-Key: td_live_your_key_here" \
  "https://api.traderdaddy.pro/api/v1/unusual-activity?minScore=85&timeFrame=today"
```

### Python
```python
import requests

API_KEY = "td_live_your_key_here"
BASE_URL = "https://api.traderdaddy.pro/api/v1"

response = requests.get(
    f"{BASE_URL}/unusual-activity",
    headers={"X-API-Key": API_KEY},
    params={"minScore": 85, "timeFrame": "today"},
)

data = response.json()
for flow in data["data"][:5]:
    print(f"{flow['ticker']} {flow['sentiment']} ${flow['premium']:,.0f}")
```

### JavaScript
```javascript
const API_KEY = "td_live_your_key_here";
const BASE_URL = "https://api.traderdaddy.pro/api/v1";

const response = await fetch(
  `${BASE_URL}/unusual-activity?minScore=85&timeFrame=today`,
  { headers: { "X-API-Key": API_KEY } }
);

const { data } = await response.json();
data.slice(0, 5).forEach((flow) => {
  console.log(`${flow.ticker} ${flow.sentiment} $${flow.premium.toLocaleString()}`);
});
```

---

## Example: wheel & dividend workflow

A common goal is monitoring a wheel / cash-secured-put / DCA income strategy. With the MCP connected, you can drive it all by asking your AI assistant — no code. Under the hood these are the tools it uses:

- **Find candidates to sell puts on:** `run_screener` with the `csp-wheel` screener → tickers set up for cash-secured puts.
- **Check if premium is worth selling right now:** `get_iv_rank` on a ticker → is implied volatility rich (good to sell) or cheap?
- **Pick a strike near a support magnet:** `get_apex_levels` → the OI/gamma "magnet" strikes and the gamma-flip level.
- **Get a ranked structure:** `get_strategy_ideas` (or `get_edge_xray` to grade the whole chain).
- **Long-term quality of the underlying** (you may get assigned shares): `get_long_term_quality` → is this a name you're happy to own?
- **Dividend capture / income timing:** `get_dividend_calendar` → ex-div dates and yields; `get_long_term/dividends` via REST for a full window.
- **Avoid event risk:** `get_earnings_flow` and `get_economic_calendar` → don't sell puts into an earnings print or an FOMC day.

Example prompt to Claude once connected:
> "Using TraderDaddy, run the csp-wheel screener, then for the top 3 names check IV rank and whether they report earnings in the next two weeks. Flag any I should avoid selling puts on right now."

---

## Notes & limits

- **Read-only.** No trading, no order placement, no account changes — market data only.
- **CORS is open** (any origin) because the API key is the auth. Keep your key private; anyone with it can use your quota.
- **User-specific in-app features are not in the public API** (e.g. saving your own screener presets). The core data endpoints all work with just your key.
- **No daily cap** beyond the per-minute limit today, but be a good citizen — cache results you re-use.

## Data usage & redistribution

This API serves TraderDaddy Pro's **analytics layer** — scores, levels, rankings,
and rollups we compute. It is deliberately **not** a market-data feed, and a few
things follow from that:

- **What you get is derived.** Unusual-activity scores and tiers, GEX and apex
  levels, conviction, sector and directional flow rollups, screener and quality
  scores, IV rank, hedge rankings, and the edge X-ray grades. This is our own
  work product, and your key licenses you to use it.
- **What you won't get, by design.** Raw option chains and per-contract
  bid/ask/greeks or per-strike IV, and third-party news article text or links.
  We license our market data from providers (including Tradier, Alpaca, and
  Finnhub) whose terms don't permit us to redistribute their raw rows, so we
  serve the layer we built on top instead. `get_edge_xray` returns rich/cheap
  and execution grades per contract rather than the quotes behind them — no
  bid/ask/mid, no per-contract IV or greeks, no open interest or volume;
  `get_premarket_gappers` returns a `hasNews` boolean rather than headline text.
  If you need a raw chain or a live quote feed, license one directly from a
  market-data vendor — that's the correct and cheaper path.
- **The one quote you do get is the underlying's.** `GET /ticker/:symbol` and
  `GET /ticker/:symbol/fundamentals` include vendor-sourced price and company
  data for the symbol you asked about, so the analytics on that response have a
  price to sit against. That is a single-symbol lookup, not a feed: it stays
  covered by the no-resell rule below, and it is not a substitute for a
  market-data subscription if what you need is streaming quotes.
- **Your use is for your own application.** Per the
  [Terms](https://www.traderdaddy.pro/terms) (§7), don't resell, sublicense, or
  redistribute the data this API returns as a data product of your own, and
  don't scrape the site. Building a tool, dashboard, bot, or research workflow
  on top of it is exactly what it's for.
- **Public-source data is exempt — but the exemption follows the SOURCE, not the
  subject.** Short interest and short volume come straight from FINRA's own
  published files, so those rows carry no restriction. Insider Form 4 activity
  and congressional disclosures are a different case: the underlying filings are
  public record and you are free to pull them yourself from SEC EDGAR or the
  House/Senate disclosure sites, but the feeds we serve are third-party
  compilations of those filings, so the rows you get from us stay covered by the
  no-resell rule above.
- **Attribution** ("Powered by TraderDaddy Pro") is appreciated but not required.

Questions about a use case that doesn't fit the above — a partnership,
white-label, or bulk arrangement — email support and ask. Some of it we can
license; some of it isn't ours to license.
